It also does work that belongs to infrastructure: it builds TypeORM queries directly, converts table rows into domain objects, and copies domain state back onto rows. For example, it writes `entity.enrolled = course.enrolled` and rebuilds an Enrolment from a row with `new Enrolment(row.courseId, row.studentEmail, row.enrolledAt)`. Converting between database rows and domain objects is a repository or adapter job. Placed in the service, it mixes ORM details into the use case. Confidence is moderate because many NestJS projects accept services calling TypeORM repositories directly.
